title: The Record: 18 students get summer internships with Pioneer
summary: Pioneer has accepted 18 college students into its summer internship program. The students come from 13 colleges and universities nationwide.
body_text: The Record: 18 students get summer internships with Pioneer 6.28.2024 "Pioneer has accepted 18 college students into its summer internship program. The students come from 13 colleges and universities nationwide, including two local to the Capital Region: University at Albany, Binghamton University, University at Buffalo, Ithaca College, St. Bonaventure University, Siena College, Bentley University, Clemson University, Endicott College, Fairfield University, Providence College, University of Richmond, and University of Tampa. The competitive ten-week internship will place the students, who are a mix of undergraduates and MBAs, in active roles throughout the organization, including consumer lending, commercial credit and retail; wealth management, IT, financial crimes and compliance; and accounting, insurance, marketing, and business analytics. All will work full-time schedules, both at Pioneer’s headquarters and its branch locations." Read the full story from The Record here.

title: Best Client Communication Platforms for Accounting Firms (July 2026)
summary: Compare the best client communication platforms for accounting firms. July 2026 rankings based on integration quality, portal features, and pricing.
body_text: You're probably chasing at least three clients right now for missing documents or approvals. Email works until it doesn't, and then you're stuck manually following up while your close timeline slides another week. Most accountants report clients respond faster when using dedicated communication platforms instead of scattered email threads. Bookkeeper client messaging platforms centralize all of that communication so clients know exactly what you need and your team can see every outstanding item at a glance. Rankings are based on real firm workflows, integration quality, and whether the pricing structure actually makes sense for practices like yours. TLDR: Client communication tools cut email clutter by centralizing document requests and messages. Best platforms sync directly with QuickBooks or Xero, letting you ask questions where work happens. Research suggests firms see faster client response times with dedicated portals versus email threads. Passwordless client access and automated reminders cut manual follow-up by hours per close cycle. Double combines client messaging, document sharing, and month-end close in one workspace. What Are Client Communication Platforms for Accounting Firms? Client communication tools for accounting firms are specialized software solutions that let bookkeepers and accountants securely interact with clients, collect documents, and ask questions without digging through email threads. At their core, these tools replace scattered back-and-forth with a centralized portal where clients can upload files, respond to requests, and view finalized reports. For the firm side, everything from document requests to transaction questions lives in one place instead of buried across inboxes. The best ones go further, connecting client communication directly to the month-end close workflow so questions get asked and answered in context, right where the actual work is happening. How We Ranked Client Communication Platforms Choosing the right tool for accounting client communication isn't straightforward, so we built our rankings around criteria that actually matter to firms. We looked at four core areas: messaging and file-sharing capabilities, client portal quality, integration with accounting software, and pricing relative to firm size. We also factored in G2 reviews to reflect real user sentiment across solo bookkeepers and multi-partner firms alike. Best Overall Client Communication Tool: Double Accounting firms increasingly rely on dedicated client communication tools to reduce email clutter, keep sensitive documents secure, and give clients a single place to stay in the loop. Double stands out here by combining a client portal, two-way messaging, document sharing, and month-end close execution into one connected workspace built for accountants and bookkeepers. Clients get a custom-branded client portal with a clean, intuitive interface where they can upload documents, respond to requests, and check the status of open items without needing to dig through email threads. On the firm side, staff can send messages, use task management to assign tasks, set deadlines, and see everything in one place instead of juggling multiple tabs. What Makes Double Worth Considering The client portal is white-labeled, so your firm's branding stays front and center instead of a third-party logo. Automated reminders nudge clients when documents or approvals are overdue, cutting down on manual follow-up. All communication is logged and searchable, which matters when you need a clear record during tax season or an audit. Integrations with popular accounting tools mean Double fits into workflows firms already use without requiring a full process overhaul. For firms tired of chasing clients over email and losing documents in inboxes, Double offers a focused, well-designed alternative worth a serious look. Canopy Canopy serves tax and accounting firms with a suite that covers client communication, document management, workflow automation, time tracking, and billing. Secure client portal with document sharing, data security, and e-signatures Workflow automation for tax and accounting projects Time tracking, billing, and CRM Mobile app for clients and staff Tax-heavy firms tend to get the most out of Canopy. The breadth works well when you need CRM and billing alongside client messaging. For bookkeeping-focused practices, though, many features may go unused. Canopy covers a wide range of firm needs under one login: a secure client portal, document storage, CRM, time tracking, billing, and workflow automation for tax and accounting practices. The CRM component tracks every client touchpoint from initial contact through invoice collection, which works well for firms running multi-step tax engagements with multiple deliverables per client per year. Workflow automation lets you build templates for recurring engagement types like tax prep or bookkeeping review, automatically assigning tasks and triggering client document requests at the right stage of the project. The mobile app gives both staff and clients access from anywhere, so clients can upload requested documents without needing to be at a desk. The client portal supports secure document sharing, e-signatures, and status visibility, keeping clients informed without requiring a phone call or email chain. Firms running primarily monthly bookkeeping engagements may find that the billing, CRM, and tax-focused features go largely unused, since the tool is built with a tax-first workflow in mind. Xenett Xenett is built for accounting firms, focusing on client collaboration and review workflows. It helps teams manage client requests, track document collection, and keep communication organized around specific tasks. Key Features Client request lists let you assign and track outstanding items directly within the workflow, reducing back-and-forth email chains asking clients what's still missing. A centralized client portal gives clients one place to upload documents, respond to queries, and see what's needed from them at any given time. Review checklists, file review tools, and task tracking keep internal teams aligned on where each client engagement stands. Xenett offers accounting workflow automation and financial close management with tools to automate review and closing processes, detect errors using AI, and support collaboration among accounting teams and clients. Xenett centers its product around financial close management, giving accounting teams a structured checklist-driven process so nothing falls through the cracks at month-end. Its AI scans for inconsistencies and coding errors before they reach the review stage, which reduces the back-and-forth that slows down close in the first place. Automation covers the repetitive steps (reconciliation validation, account balance checks, and flagging transactions that deviate from historical patterns) so senior staff spend time on exceptions instead of routine verification. Clients and internal teams share the same close workspace, meaning everyone sees which items are pending and who owns each task without a status meeting. For firms running standardized close processes across a large client base, this consistency is a real advantage. That said, client communication in Xenett sits at the checklist level instead of the transaction level, so asking a client about a specific line item means stepping outside the close workflow instead of tagging it inline. Financial Cents Financial Cents tracks bookkeeping projects visually, with workflow automation and task lists keeping client work moving without constant manual nudging. What They Offer Automated data collection that pulls in what you need without chasing clients for every document Staff collaboration and time tracking so everyone knows who owns what and where work stands Invoice-ready data exports that make billing straightforward at the end of an engagement Custom client performance reports you can share directly with clients to show progress Financial Cents covers the day-to-day needs of bookkeeping and accounting firms from client onboarding through invoice collection. Automated data collection sends requests to clients on a schedule and tracks which documents have come in, so the team spends less time manually chasing outstanding items. Project boards give every staff member a clear view of where each client engagement stands, with task assignments and due dates that keep work moving without a daily check-in meeting. Time tracking runs alongside projects instead of as a separate step, capturing billable hours as work happens so billing data is ready when the engagement closes. Custom financial performance reports can be built and shared directly with clients, giving bookkeepers a straightforward way to show progress and surface trends over time. For firms that manage a high volume of monthly clients and want one place to coordinate their team, collect documents, and monitor client health, Financial Cents brings those workflows into a single view. A few things that stand out about Financial Cents: Automated data collection requests reduce the back-and-forth of chasing clients for documents. Project tracking gives staff visibility into where each engagement stands. Custom reports let firms monitor client financial performance over time. TaxDome TaxDome covers both internal firm operations and client-facing work in a single tool, making it one of the more complete options for tax and accounting practices. CRM and workflow automation for managing client engagements and internal tasks Secure document storage with e-signatures and proposal tools built in Client messaging, invoicing, and payment collection through a dedicated portal Mobile access for both clients and staff TaxDome suits firms that want one login for nearly everything. It skews toward tax practices, so bookkeeping-first firms may find the feature set broader than what they need. For a detailed side-by-side, read the Double vs TaxDome comparison . TaxDome manages both internal processes including workflow, CRM, reporting, and secure document storage, plus client-facing activities like documents, signatures, invoicing, messages, and proposals, available on desktop or mobile. TaxDome runs internal firm operations and client-facing work through a single login, with visual workflow pipelines that move jobs through defined stages and trigger pre-set actions automatically. On the internal side, you get CRM tracking, team reporting, secure document storage, and pre-built templates for common tax and accounting engagements. Client-facing tools cover secure document exchange, e-signatures, invoicing, messaging, and proposal delivery, all accessible from desktop or the mobile app, so clients can upload documents or sign off on items without being tied to a desk. Integrations with QuickBooks Online, Zapier, Stripe, Outlook, Calendly, and major tax programs fit most existing firm tech stacks without a full overhaul. According to TaxDome, client portal stickiness is strong: 90% of clients who log in once continue using it, and client bases grew 22% year-over-year in 2025. For bookkeeping-focused practices, the QuickBooks integration only syncs invoices and payments in one direction, which means toggling between systems during month-end close and adding an extra step that a two-way sync connection removes entirely. Firms using dedicated client communication tools report faster response times and higher client satisfaction scores. Double's clean inbox keeps every client conversation organized by engagement, so nothing slips through the cracks. Automated reminders nudge clients on outstanding document requests, and a branded client portal gives your firm a professional, polished presence without any extra setup.

The SBRG Program provides funds to benefit the small businesses of FHLBNY members, including farms and non-profit organizations. Through the SBRG Program, members can provide grants of up to $10,000 to qualifying small businesses that have faced economic challenges due to the rate environment, inflation, supply-chain constraints, and/or rising energy costs. "Our partnership with the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York continues to create opportunities to make a meaningful difference in the communities we serve," said Leonardo Ramos, First Vice President, CRA Officer, Provident Bank. "These recovery grants provide valuable resources that help local nonprofit organizations expand their impact, strengthen their operations, and continue delivering critical services to individuals and families." As a dedicated member of the FHLBNY, Provident Bank continues to actively invest in the economic vitality of its local neighborhoods by ensuring small businesses and non-profits have the resources necessary to continue thriving. The following non-profit organizations received grants through the FHLBNY SBRG Program: Bloom Empower - $5,000 LISC NJ - $10,000 Mercer County Community College Foundation - $5,000 New Life Community Development Corporation - $10,000 Rising Tide Capital - $10,000 SAFE in Hunterdon - $10,000 About Provident Bank Founded in Jersey City in 1839, Provident Bank is the oldest community-focused financial institution based in New Jersey and is the wholly owned subsidiary of Provident Financial Services, Inc. body_text: MALVERN, Pa., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ocugen, Inc. (Ocugen or the Company) (NASDAQ: OCGN), a pioneering biotechnology leader in gene therapies for blindness diseases, today announced that it will host a conference call and live webcast to discuss the Company’s second quarter 2026 financial results and provide a business update at 8:30 a.m. ET on Thursday, August 6, 2026. Ocugen will issue a pre-market earnings announcement on the same day. Attendees are invited to participate on the call using the following details: Dial-in Numbers : (800) 715-9871 for U.S. callers and (646) 307-1963 for international callers Conference ID : 2222566 Webcast : Available on the events section of the Ocugen investor site A replay of the call and archived webcast will be available on the Ocugen investor site . About Ocugen, Inc. Ocugen, Inc. is a pioneering biotechnology company developing gene therapies for blindness. The Company’s breakthrough modifier gene therapy platform has the potential to address significant unmet medical needs across large patient populations through a gene-agnostic approach. Unlike traditional gene therapies and gene-editing technologies that target a single gene mutation, Ocugen’s modifier gene therapies are designed to address the underlying disease biology by restoring balance across multiple gene networks. The Company is currently advancing programs for inherited retinal diseases and other causes of blindness that affect millions worldwide, including retinitis pigmentosa, Stargardt disease, and geographic atrophy, an advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration. Discover more at www.ocugen.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X .
